title: Testing Interface Implementations
story: You implemented the `Validator` interface for five different types. But are they all correct? An email validator that accepts '@@' is broken. A password checker that allows empty strings is dangerous. Systematically test interface implementations to catch these bugs.
why: Interfaces create contracts between code — testing implementations ensures every type satisfies the interface correctly and behaves as expected.
analogy: When you buy a phone charger, you expect it to fit any USB-C port — that's the interface specification. Testing interface implementations is like a quality inspector verifying every charger from every manufacturer fits every port, delivers correct voltage, and doesn't short circuit.
try_it: Create a `RangeChecker` that checks if a value is between min and max (inclusive). Write tests for: value at min, value at max, value below min, value above max, and negative ranges. Run each test through a single `test_checker[T: Checker]` function.
tips: Test both success and failure paths for every implementation
Edge cases reveal bugs: empty input, boundary values, extreme values
Write a generic test runner that works with any interface implementation
common_mistakes: Testing only valid inputs — invalid inputs are where bugs hide
Not checking error_message is non-empty — silent failures are confusing
Testing only one implementation and assuming others work the same way
